items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1958-08-08; 1958-09-03
items.q: George Fields, trombone man. And they sitting on the bandstand, he told me.

ctx.x: Do you remember about what years you played with the imperial band?

I guess I could. That's how I come together with Ori, playing with the imperial band. George Fields, they said, they got a young fella just come here from Mountain or Plats, Louisiana, named Ori. And he said, they got a little band. He said, you be just a guy for them guys. He said, they need a bass man. He said, go on down there and help them out. Join them. Play with them, help them out. He said, I think they got something. And that's true for me how they have them. George Fields, trombone man. And they sitting…
Yeah. I never did meet him.

Then the next band went, Big Eye Lewy. He come along. Big Eye Lewy was with Freddie and, uh, and-and-and-and George Backe was with, uh, And, uh, George Fields was with Manuel. Then when I was at the Dreamland, I went to Wake Down and Peekin for Dan Jackson, and I used to have Manuel, Teo, Frankie Enya, see, and, uh, Eddie Atkins on some bones.

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: So many of them I worked with a lot of good ones and a lot of bad ones.

ctx.x: The trombone players, which trombone Players do you remember that you enjoyed working with?

There you are again. Poor me, (unintelligible). So many of them I worked with a lot of good ones and a lot of bad ones. You know. I got to give all -- old Red the devil, which belongs to him. Ory, and I got to give Eddie Atkins, I got to give Honore Dutrey -- I'm calling trombone players. George Fields --
